slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: One ruler for many nations? Genesis pictures nations obeying a ruler from Judah. Jesus speaks of other sheep joining one flock under one shepherd.
slides.body: Genesis pictures nations obeying a ruler from Judah. Jesus speaks of other sheep joining one flock under one shepherd.
slides.heading: One ruler for many nations?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Gen 49:10: The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes and the allegiance of the nations is his.
slides.body: The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes and the allegiance of the nations is his.
slides.heading: Gen 49:10

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Jn 10:16, BSB: I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them in as well, and they will listen to My voice. Then there will be one flock and one shepherd.
slides.body: I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them in as well, and they will listen to My voice. Then there will be one flock and one shepherd.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Jn 10:16

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Why Christians connect them Both passages picture people gathering under one leader. Christians see Jesus bringing people from outside Israel into the community he leads.
slides.body: Both passages picture people gathering under one leader. Christians see Jesus bringing people from outside Israel into the community he leads.
slides.heading: Why Christians connect them

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But the pictures are not identical John never quotes Genesis here. A flock listening to one shepherd is not the same as nations obeying a king. The ideas are similar, but the match does not identify Jesus by itself.
slides.body: John never quotes Genesis here. A flock listening to one shepherd is not the same as nations obeying a king. The ideas are similar, but the match does not identify Jesus by itself.
slides.heading: But the pictures are not identical

title: Do Jesus’s “other sheep” fulfil the allegiance of the nations?
